title: Micro-probe config cascade for safe batching & KV-caching tuning
creator: Aisha Navarro
description:
Problem statement:
We want to automatically recommend and safely apply batching and KV-cache configurations per customer workload to reduce per-token cost, without risking SLO regressions. Prior approaches applied coarse, global config changes and relied on broad canaries; these occasionally produced transient latency spikes and noisy throughput regressions for specific tenant cohorts.

Goal:
Build a micro-probing and config-cascade orchestration that: 1) recommends candidate batching/prefetch/cache settings per traffic cohort, 2) applies them in controlled micro-probes (small percentage of traffic, per-cohort), 3) observes fused regression signals (latency P95/P99, tail CPU/GPU stall, queue depth, and error rate), and 4) automatically escalates to wider rollouts or instant rollback when deterministic guards trigger.

Design summary (high level):
- Recommendation engine: offline job suggests 3 candidate profiles per cohort (conservative/medium/aggressive) using historical sequence-length distribution, prefix-hit-rates, and token-cost model. Stored in config-store: /configs/auto-tune/{cohort}/{profile}.
- Micro-probe launcher: staged traffic allocation with a "probe window" (default 5m) and a "stabilization window" (default 15m). Each probe is limited to max 0.5% global traffic or 5 RPS per cohort (whichever smaller).
- Config cascade: apply profile to progressively larger cohorts by inheritance and isolation rules. When a cohort-level probe fails, quarantine that cohort and attempt a narrowed probe (e.g., split by route or user-agent). The cascade prevents global blast radius by ensuring parent configs never automatically replace conservative parents unless all children succeed.
- SLO-aware limiters and routing: integrate with the runtime's smart-router to temporarily steer riskier requests to a fallback model variant or a dedicated fast-path when probe signals approach SLO thresholds. Limiters include per-cohort max in-flight, dynamic throttle based on observed P99 delta, and token-budget windows to prevent queue spikes.
- Anomaly detection & fused signals: combine statistical drift detectors on latency/throughput with resource signals (GPU util, kernel stalls) and business signals (error rate, user-facing timeouts). Use rule-based thresholds plus a lightweight ML ensemble to reduce false-positives during naturally bursty traffic.
- Deterministic rollback policy: 3 independent triggers that immediately rollback a probe: latency breach (P99 > baseline + 40%), queue growth (>3x baseline within 2m), error spike (>2x baseline 5xx within 5m). If two out of three fire, trigger fast rollback and human alert.

Telemetry and observability:
- New dashboards: per-probe view (latency, throughput, cache hit-rate, GPU stall, queue depth), probe heatmap across cohorts, and a global "config-cascade" timeline. Links: internal dash (https://dash.redwood.ai/d/config-cascade).
- Traces: add probe-id tag to existing tracing so we can slice traces by probe and produce flamegraphs for tail latency investigations.
- Alerts: brief anomaly alerts for threshold-exceeds and consolidated rollback alert to oncall with runbook link.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary on staging with synthetic workload that simulates multi-tenancy and cold caches (target: identify false positive triggers).
2) Internal canary: 1 customer (team-internal) and 2 non-critical tenants at 0.1% traffic. Monitor for 48h.
3) Gradual wider rollout: increase probe share following success gates (no rollback, stable P95/P99) across cohorts.
4) Full automation opt-in: initially manual-approve for each tenant; after 6 weeks of safe runs, enable auto-approve for low-risk tenants.

Acceptance criteria:
- Recommendation engine suggests candidate profiles for 95% of tenant routes with plausible cost delta estimates.
- Micro-probe system can execute probes with <500ms additional orchestration latency and respect configured traffic limits.
- Automatic rollback fires and completes within 30s when deterministic triggers occur.
- Observability: probe dashboards accurately tag >99% of probe traffic and make root-cause traces accessible within 2 clicks.

Artifacts and references:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/MicroProbe+Config+Cascade
- Draft PR (runtime change): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4148
- Telemetry proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/commit/2b7f9e

Open trade-offs and risks:
- Probe granularity vs. signal strength: very small probes reduce blast radius but increase false-positives due to noisy signals. We mitigate with ensemble detection and stabilization windows.
- Complexity of per-cohort config store and inheritance: more operational overhead and migration of existing configs. We will provide migration tooling that marks replaced configs and supports rollback.
- Risk of cascading failures if routing fallback capacity is insufficient. Plan: reserve a small pool of fallback capacity for probes and monitor its utilization.

Next steps (short-term):
- Spike: implement probe-id propagation and probe metric collection (2 wks).
- Implement deterministic rollback hooks and basic orchestrator with config-store integration (3 wks).
- End-to-end staging run and internal canary (2 wks).
